claim: The supplier specifies storing Invitrogen F8801 microspheres refrigerated at 2-8 degrees Celsius, protected from light.

identifiers.product: FluoSpheres Carboxylate-Modified Microspheres, 0.1 um, red fluorescent (580/605)
identifiers.applies_to: the type F8801. Applying it to the beads on this bench goes through the E5 linking claim particle_suspension_b_identity, which a card applying this to the bench must cite alongside it and which fixes the grade at E5 by 5.8

validity_conditions: A SUPPLIER SPECIFICATION, NOT A LABORATORY LIMIT. 'The supplier says 2-8 C, protect from light' is knowledge; how this laboratory stores its bottle is policy and belongs to a person. Nothing here is an envelope value or a ceiling any mechanism enforces. Kelvin because the unit registry cannot carry an offset unit, and 275/281 K rather than 275.15/281.15 K so as not to claim five figures from bounds given to the nearest degree -- the same choice tracer_storage_conditions made. Whether this bottle has been kept that way, or frozen, is unrecorded. THIS IS ABOUT THE TYPE, NOT THE BOTTLE. Under the instance/type split, F8801 is a type and its facts are ordinary entries at E3 from the supplier; the beads on the bench are the instance particle_suspension_b, and the claim joining them is particle_suspension_b_identity at E5, because the person named the product by pasting this page and did not read the bottle. Anything here applied to the bench inherits E5. READ BY THIS SEAT, NOT ONLY PASTED. The person's paste (microscope_agent/questions/mic-20260930-001/asked_of_the_person.jsonl at 51c61eb) is what identified the product; the values here were read by this seat off the vendor's own page on 2026-10-01 and agree with the paste on every field, which is why this is spec: at E3 and not a copy of a copy.
